beats.text: Seventy five men applied for 24 places.
beats.note: The advert asked for male college students for a study of prison life, paying $15 a day for one to two weeks from 14 August 1971.

beats.text: A two week study ended on day six.
beats.note: Psychologist Christina Maslach visited, was troubled by how participants were behaving and being treated, and confronted Philip Zimbardo.

beats.text: The guards were told what to create.
beats.note: Thibault Le Texier's 2019 paper quotes the orientation: We can create boredom. We can create a sense of frustration.

beats.text: One guard said he was directed to act.
beats.note: Guard 11 wrote in 1971 that the team specifically directed him to act a certain way. On tape, the warden told guards: we need you to play the part of tough guard.

beats.text: The book says they had no formal training.
beats.note: Zimbardo wrote that the guards were told primarily to maintain law and order. Le Texier argues they knew what results were wanted and how to achieve them.

beats.context: how long the study ran, against a plan of one to two weeks.
